sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: *Nem* stays right before the verb, even after *miért*: *Miért nem főzöl?* means “Why don’t you cook?” The reason follows with *mert*: *Mert olvasok.*

sections.title: One sentence
sections.content: In one sentence it is *Nem főzök, mert olvasok.* The comma goes before *mert*. *Miért?* alone is a full question after a *nem*: *Nem főzök. – Miért?*

sections.title: Nem … mert …
rows: I do not cook, because I read.
I do not walk, because I study.
Anna does not write, because she reads.
Meg does not study, because she cooks.

items.english: I do not walk, because I study.

sections.content: Keep *nem* before the verb: *Nem főzök*, not *Főzök nem*.
